questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: Nature

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Academic level, opportunities not available in Denmark

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was fine

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I cannot remember but remember the overall experience as smooth

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Very hard. I used facebook market place and wrote to a bunch of people. Only got a place because the guy who was renting it out had the same name as me. Expect to pay more than on campus. Look for places close to the buses such as R4 or 99. Try and find someone to search with.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is expensive.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Not satisfied since most of the people got in on campus and it was hard having to live of campus alone.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is confusing

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You send a list of 10 courses before going but you cant really find any course descriptions. Upon arrival you will gradually be registered on some courses and maybe on waitlist. You dont know if you will get in of the wait list and in the beginning you might have to follow along many classes due to this uncertainty.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Not really any help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got accepted to all the classes I was waitlisted on so overall very succesfull.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Look at the schedules and try and see if anything have been written about the course online on sites like reddit or similar. Some courses have a bad rep.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took 4 300 level courses. I would say cpsc340 was really time consuming but als really rewarding. cpsc330 was a lot easier but still time consuming at times. cpsc322 was interesting. cpsc314 was overall easy. Overall spent more time on homework than anticipated but most of it was worth it due to the level of education.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very similar. I had lectures and mandatory assignments. The assignments counts toward your final grade which is nice. Did not really use the lab sessions as it was just dedicated time to do assignments. My exams/midterms were all either with a cheatsheet or with no help (cpsc314)

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
cpsc340
cpsc330
cpsc322
cpsc312

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you want to learn ML from the ground then definitely 340. By far the most time consuming course but the proff Jeff is fantastic and you have so many aha-moments. If you combine it with cpsc330 which is applied ML then 330 becomes a lot easier. In 330 you learn specifically how to go from dataset to ML-model whereas 340 is more theory based. If you want to have more freetime then skip 340.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Hmm nothing really unexpected.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Shopping for everyday food is quite expensive. Phone plans are also expensive I was able to just keep my danish number due to an old sweet deal with my carrier.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I did not really use the clubs to much but the surf club has a sweet trip, VOC plan trips and have gear for rent and the ski club has free rental skies which is awesome. I thought about joining a soccer league but I was never home during the weekends anyway due to hiking trips and similar.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Really anything you like. They had a quidditch club for example.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: If you live on or close to campus then start a morning swimming "club" at wreck beach. Really nice way to start the day. Look out on the various clubs instagram pages for events - they sometimes plan parties and trips and you might want to join a club for one particular trip only which is totally fine.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go explore the mountains. Hike in the summer and ski in the winter. Buy the student ski pass. Get to Vancouver Island. Get to Seattle and watch an nfl game. Watch a hockey game. But mostly the mountain stuff

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: No it is pretty easy just be open minded and if you want to make friends then show up for social activities and take initiative to plan get togethers.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: It can be a bit difficult to adjust to the amount of small talking but nothing major.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
- You have a the time and money. You think you cant join the weekend trip because it is a bit too expensive or you have an assignment due. You will find the time somehow. Just go and figure it out afterwards.
- Get out and explore the city/nature
- Pray you get in to on campus housing

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer:
If you are looking for great study spots: I found that the upper floor of the pharma building had some really nice spots to sit a few together. Otherwise if you are alone and just want to grind go to the basement of koerners library. 
The busses/trains are great and you can pay directly with apple pay until you get your upass.
Sign up for evo and turo for car renting.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting out into some crazy nature.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to living off campus alone while a lot of my friends lived on campus with others

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
